_doc: TCCC equipment/tool detection ontology for the TC3-VQA detection layer. Classes are clinically salient, visually distinguishable in a still, and present in instructional/field footage. Each class lists a short visual description (so a vision annotator boxes the right object) and the TCCC concept(s) it co-occurs with. Auto-annotated by a vision LLM, independently verified, physician spot-checked.

classes.desc: windlass/CAT-style limb tourniquet on an extremity: a wide strap with a windlass rod and securing clip
junctional/pelvic tourniquet device (rigid frame/pads at groin or axilla), distinct from a limb strap
hemostatic/combat gauze or rolled dressing being packed into or held over a wound
elastic/emergency pressure bandage (e.g., Israeli/OLAES) wrapped over a dressing
NPA: a soft curved nasal tube with a flared flange, near or inserted in a nostril
cricothyroidotomy tube / bougie / surgical-airway kit at the anterior neck
scalpel or blade held to make an incision
occlusive/vented chest seal (adhesive square/disc) on the chest
needle-decompression catheter/large-bore needle inserted into the anterior/lateral chest
IV catheter or intraosseous (IO) needle/driver inserted into or held against the skin/bone
syringe (with or without needle), e.g., drawing or administering medication
TCCC casualty card / DD-1380 documentation card
marker/pen used to write a time or note (on a tourniquet, card, or skin)
trauma shears/scissors cutting clothing or gauze
provider hand(s) performing the intervention (gloved or bare)

rules: Box only objects that are CLEARLY visible and identifiable; do not guess occluded/ambiguous items.
One box per distinct instance; box the object tightly.
Do NOT box the casualty's body or wounds (handled by the anatomy/region layer), except gloved_hands.
Burned-in captions/logos are masked in the released frames and are not objects.
